stories.headline: Red Flag Warning Declared; Dangerous Fire Conditions Expected This Week as Cold Front Arrives
stories.summary: The National Weather Service declared a Red Flag Warning Saturday, February 21 for most of North Central Florida — including neighboring Alachua and Gilchrist counties — as extreme wildfire conditions intensify across the region. A strong cold front moving through Florida this weekend will usher in dangerously low humidity levels and wind gusts exceeding 30 mph on Monday and Tuesday, a deadly combination with bone-dry vegetation left from months of extreme drought. Any fire that starts under these conditions could spread out of control rapidly. Overnight temperatures are expected to drop into the upper 20s to low 30s across North Florida by mid-week. Columbia County's burn ban remains in effect, and residents are urged to avoid all outdoor burning. High Sunday in Fort White: 71°F with scattered showers, dropping sharply to a high of only 49°F on Monday as cold air arrives.

stories.headline: SR-47 Through Fort White to Close Tuesday and Wednesday for Road Work; Hal Adams Bridge Also Closed
stories.summary: The Florida Department of Transportation announced multiple road closures in Columbia County for the week of February 21–27. State Road 47 — the main highway running through Fort White — will have daytime lane closures on Tuesday and Wednesday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. for road work between Clay Hole Creek and Southwest Main Boulevard. The Hal Adams Bridge on State Road 51, which crosses the Suwannee River, faces daytime closures Monday through February 28 for bridge repair. Additional nighttime closures are planned on I-75 at County Road 341 (Tuesday and Wednesday, 9:30 p.m.–4:30 a.m.) and at US-90 (Monday, 9:30 p.m.–4:30 a.m.). US-41 at Howell Road will also see weekday closures for traffic signal work. Drivers traveling through the area should plan for delays and allow extra travel time.

stories.headline: Should Fort White Cease to Exist? The Full Story Behind the Town's Dissolution Fight
stories.summary: Fort White — chartered in 1957 and one of Columbia County's smallest incorporated towns — has been locked in a months-long political battle over whether it should dissolve itself and hand governance over to Columbia County. The conflict started in December 2025, when Mayor George Thomas walked out of a council meeting after four council members voted to strip him of his presiding officer role — a move Thomas called 'ridiculous and silly behavior' in a letter to residents. The tension escalated in January when those same four members voted to schedule a special dissolution workshop over the Mayor's sole objection. On February 5, Columbia County commissioners weighed in, with Commissioner Rocky Ford insisting the county needed to be involved — though commissioners have no legal authority to block a dissolution vote. The Feb. 18 workshop, packed with roughly 140 people, became the defining moment: financial consultant Richard Powell presented five years of data showing the town has zero debt and grew its reserves from eight months of expenditures to sixteen months — a clean bill of health. When Mayor Thomas asked for a show of hands of Town residents who wanted to dissolve Fort White, not a single hand went up. The workshop's instigator, Councilman Bill Koon — notably a Columbia County employee — had previously tried to pass a dissolution resolution without public notice. Despite the overwhelming opposition, a first reading of an ordinance to dissolve the town is still on the agenda for Monday's council meeting, February 23 at 6 PM at the Fort White Community Center. Fort White has 411 registered voters and collects no property taxes, operating entirely on state grants and revenue sharing.

stories.headline: Florida Extreme Drought Coverage Grows 24% in One Week; All of State Now in Drought
stories.summary: According to a WUFT News report published Thursday, February 19, the area of Florida covered by extreme drought grew by nearly 24 percent compared to the prior week's U.S. Drought Monitor report, expanding into Volusia, Lake, and several South Florida counties including Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade. As of February 19, 87.5 percent of Florida is under severe drought conditions — up from 85.5 percent the prior week — and all of the state is experiencing at least some level of drought. Only two tiny areas remain classified as merely 'abnormally dry': the northern Brevard County coastline and the immediate coast of Miami-Dade. Meteorologists attribute the worsening conditions to a La Niña winter pattern, a lack of major rain events, and persistent high pressure that both limited rainfall and drove up temperatures. Long-term models show below-average rainfall likely through May; a cold front approaching Sunday is expected to bring some rain but will not meaningfully relieve drought conditions in Columbia County or North Florida.

stories.headline: 140 Residents Pack Fort White Forum; Financial Consultant Gives Town Clean Bill of Health
stories.summary: About 140 people — residents, non-residents, and county officials — packed the Fort White Community Center on Tuesday, February 17 for a special workshop on whether to dissolve the town. Former Columbia County auditor Richard 'Dick' Powell, invited by Mayor George Thomas, gave a surprise presentation showing the town's fund balance grew from eight months of expenditures to sixteen months over five years, and that the town carries zero debt. When Mayor Thomas asked for a show of hands from Town residents who wanted to dissolve Fort White, not a single hand went up. County Commission Chair Tim Murphy and other prominent county figures attended the meeting, which was initiated by Councilman Bill Koon — a Columbia County employee — who had previously tried to pass a dissolution resolution without public notice. Fort White has 411 registered voters, according to the Supervisor of Elections.

stories.headline: Lady Indians Fall to Hilliard in Region 3-R Championship; Season Ends at 17-10
stories.summary: The Fort White Lady Indians' season came to an end Friday night in Hilliard, as the No. 2-seeded Indians fell to top-seeded Hilliard 56-37 in the Region 3-R girls basketball championship — a rematch of last year's regional final loss. Jahlaya Wilson led Fort White with 15 points, 7 rebounds, and 5 blocks, but the Indians could not contain Hilliard senior Alyssa Hallman, who scored 31 points after being held scoreless in the first quarter. Fort White trailed 30-20 at halftime and could not mount a sustained comeback. Head coach Bregay Harris expressed confidence in the team's future, noting several key players are juniors with high-level AAU opportunities ahead. The Flashes (24-5) advance to their second consecutive state semifinal. Fort White finishes 17-10.

stories.headline: Fort White Seeking Town Attorney Amid Dissolution Debate and Open Town Clerk Position
stories.summary: The Town of Fort White has issued a Request for Proposal for Town Attorney legal services, accepting sealed proposals until 4 p.m. at the Town Clerk's Office. Submissions may be made by mail to P.O. Box 129, Fort White, FL 32038, by email, or in person at 118 SW Wilson Springs Road. Interested parties must submit one original, five copies, and one digital copy — all clearly marked 'Town Attorney Legal Services.' The search for legal counsel comes as Fort White simultaneously has a vacancy for Town Clerk and faces a continuing public debate over whether to dissolve the town into Columbia County. The next Town Council meeting is Monday, February 23 at 6 p.m. at the Fort White Community Center.

stories.headline: FHSAA Merges Rural and Class 1A Football; Fort White Indians Assigned to New District
stories.summary: The Florida High School Athletic Association voted 11-1 on Thursday, January 29 to merge the Rural and Class 1A football classifications for the 2026 and 2027 seasons. The emergency board meeting was called after a sudden wave of Rural schools — including Union County and Dixie County — switched to the Sunshine State Athletic Association (SSAA), shrinking the Rural class from 32 to just 16 schools. Fort White, which was one of five Gainesville-area teams remaining in the Rural class, will now compete in Class 1A football alongside former Rural rivals. FHSAA released new 2026–28 district assignments on Friday, February 13, placing Fort White in a district with Lafayette (Mayo), Madison County, and Taylor County. The Rural classification will remain in place for all other sports.

stories.headline: Indians Win First Game of Season, Beat Bell 12-7 on the Road
stories.summary: The Fort White Indians picked up their first win of the 2026 baseball season Thursday night, defeating the Bell Bulldogs 12-7 on the road. The Indians outhit Bell 14 to 7 en route to the victory, with sophomore Aaron Parnell going 3-for-5 with 3 RBI and senior Elias Byrd going 2-for-3. Fort White improves to 1-4 on the season. The Indians return home Monday, February 23 to host the Hamilton County Trojans at 7:00 PM.

stories.headline: Columbia County Commission to Vote on TD Bank Building Purchase for Tax Collector's Office
stories.summary: The Columbia County Board of Commissioners is set to vote Thursday night on whether to complete the purchase of the old TD Bank building in downtown Lake City to house the growing Tax Collector's Office. According to the Lake City Reporter, an inspection of the building showed no major structural issues. The commission meets at 6:00 PM at the School Board Administrative Complex Auditorium.

stories.headline: New Olustee Battlefield Museum Breaks Ground at State Park
stories.summary: A new museum at Olustee Battlefield Historic State Park broke ground during last weekend's 49th Annual Battle of Olustee Re-enactment festivities. State Rep. Chuck Brannan attended the groundbreaking ceremony alongside a rendering of the planned facility. The museum will feature indoor and outdoor exhibits interpreting Florida's Civil War history and the events leading to the 1864 Battle of Olustee, the largest Civil War engagement fought in Florida. The state park is located on US-90, about 13 miles east of Lake City.

stories.headline: Fort White Council Finds No Support to Dissolve Town; Ordinance Reading Set for Monday
stories.summary: Fort White council members and residents rejected the idea of dissolving the town into Columbia County at a packed special meeting Tuesday night at the Fort White Community Center. Both the public and council members voiced opposition to dissolution. Mayor George Thomas, who was the lone vote against holding the special meeting, echoed residents' sentiments. Councilman Bill Koon read from prepared notes during the session. Despite the lack of support, a first reading of an ordinance to dissolve the town remains on next Monday's (February 23) agenda, though its future is uncertain following the discussions.

stories.headline: All North-Central Florida Counties Now at Extreme Drought; Experts Warn of Months More
stories.summary: Every county in north-central Florida is now under extreme drought conditions, according to the latest U.S. Drought Monitor analysis. Despite parts of the area receiving over an inch of rain on February 15, the region remains far behind on rainfall for the water year. Gainesville has received just 25% of its usual rainfall since January, while Ocala has received only 18%. Alachua Conservation Trust fire specialist Nathan Bullian warned of a direct correlation between the drought and wildfire incidents, with more than 600 wildfires burning about 16,000 acres statewide from January to February 8. Two water management districts have declared Phase I Moderate Water Shortages, asking residents to voluntarily reduce water use.

stories.headline: Lake City Man Arrested on Child Pornography Charges
stories.summary: Joshua Lee Hoger, 30, of Lake City was arrested Thursday after Columbia County Sheriff's Office detectives found over 20 images and videos of child sexual abuse material on his computer. The investigation began January 26 when the North Florida Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force received a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. After tracing the case to a Lake City address and serving search warrants, authorities recovered evidence and issued an arrest warrant. Hoger was booked into the Columbia County Detention Facility on charges of using a two-way communication device to commit a felony and possession of child pornography. The investigation is ongoing and more charges could be filed.

stories.headline: Wildfire Response Ramps Up Across North Florida; Air Tankers Staged in Lake City
stories.summary: The Florida Forest Service has moved large air tankers to Lake City as wildfire response intensifies across North Florida. According to News4Jax, Jacksonville Fire Rescue has responded to 29 wildfire incidents so far this year — more than double the 13 from the same period last year. In Duval County alone, the Forest Service has gone from 1 fire on 1 acre at this point last year to 11 fires on 50 acres. Four tractor plow units are now dedicated to Duval County. Officials urge residents to clear vegetation away from homes, trim bushes and trees, rake leaves several feet from structures, and clean roofs and gutters since fire travels by air as well as by ground.

stories.headline: Two Arrested in Lake City Undercover Child Predator Operation; One Suspect From Fort White
stories.summary: Two men face charges after Lake City police conducted an undercover operation to catch online child predators. Joseph Anderson, 25, of Chiefland and Robert Smith, 38, of Fort White were arrested after attempting to arrange meetings with who they believed were underage girls — but were actually undercover detectives. Anderson was arrested Monday and Smith was taken into custody on Tuesday. Both men engaged in sexually explicit conversations before arranging the meetings, according to police.

stories.headline: Drought Worsens Across Northeast Florida Despite Sunday's Storms
stories.summary: Despite Sunday's severe weather, Northeast Florida's drought situation remains dire. According to News4Jax meteorologist Katie Garner, the region is sitting at 'severe drought' — just one step below 'extreme.' The storms on February 15 barely made a dent in the rainfall deficit. Fire risk remains elevated, with dry conditions making it easier for wildfires to start and spread. Light winds of 5–10 mph and mild temperatures around 69°F are expected early this week.

stories.headline: National Wildfire Prevention Team Deployed to Florida Amid Growing Fire Risk
stories.summary: The National Wildfire Prevention and Education team has arrived in Florida for a two-week assignment to raise awareness about wildfire risk as drought conditions worsen. According to the Florida Forest Service, human activity causes 80% of wildfires — including outdoor cooking, campfires, yard debris burning, and even sparks from vehicle maintenance issues like low tire pressure or towing chains. About 95% of Florida is experiencing at least moderate drought, with severe drought conditions across Central and North Florida. Residents are urged not to burn anything outdoors and to clear vegetation away from homes.

stories.headline: Severe Storms and Tornado Watch Hit Northeast Florida Sunday
stories.summary: A strong cold front brought severe storms across Northeast Florida on Sunday, February 15, prompting a tornado watch through 8 p.m. The Storm Prediction Center placed the region at a Level 2 (Slight Risk) for severe weather. A Wind Advisory was in effect for areas west of the St. Johns River as south winds gusted up to 35–45 mph. The main squall line moved through western counties between 2–3 p.m. and reached inland Northeast Florida counties including Baker, Bradford, Clay, and Alachua by 4–5 p.m. The threat diminished by late evening as the cold front pushed through.

stories.headline: 47th Annual Olustee Festival Draws Crowds to Lake City
stories.summary: Lake City hosted the 47th Annual Olustee Festival over Presidents' Day weekend at Wilson Park on Lake DeSoto, commemorating the 1864 Battle of Olustee — the largest Civil War engagement fought in Florida. The festival, held annually since 1976, featured over 150 vendors, food trucks, a children's area, local entertainment, and homemade arts and crafts from across the country. Road closures were in effect around downtown Lake City. The festival ran Friday and Saturday, February 13–14, from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

stories.headline: Wildfires Surge Across Florida as Drought Reaches 25-Year High
stories.summary: Florida is experiencing its worst drought in 25 years, with the Florida Forest Service reporting more than 650 wildfires and over 21,000 acres burned since January 1, 2026. According to Fox Weather, 98% of the state is under some level of drought, with 85% in severe drought — the most since March 2001. Emergency burn bans are active in 34 of 67 counties, including Columbia County. A wildfire in Marion County forced the closure of State Road 19 between CR-314 and SR-40, with detours in place.

stories.headline: Gov. DeSantis Declares State of Emergency Over Drought and Cold Weather
stories.summary: Governor Ron DeSantis signed Executive Order 26-33 on Monday, February 9 declaring a state of emergency due to worsening drought and the impact of recent cold weather on Florida agriculture. The order provides emergency support for farmers, waives agricultural weight restrictions for crop transport, and directs the state to seek federal aid from the USDA and Small Business Administration. The Suwannee River Water Management District, which includes Columbia County, has an ongoing water shortage advisory citing an average rainfall deficit of nearly 11.5 inches across 14 of its 15 counties.

stories.headline: Rep. Cammack Hosts Farm Bill Listening Session at Santa Fe River Ranch
stories.summary: Congresswoman Kat Cammack hosted an agricultural listening session on Friday, February 13 at the Santa Fe River Ranch in North Central Florida, hours before a draft of the 2026 Farm Bill was released. Cammack highlighted wins including long-term funding to combat Citrus Greening disease, increased block grants for Florida farmers, and specialty crop innovation. She also noted additional disaster relief funding is on the way for farmers impacted by tariffs and recent freezing temperatures, and pushed for the expansion of broadband and water infrastructure in rural communities.

stories.headline: 49th Annual Battle of Olustee Re-enactment Wraps Up
stories.summary: The 49th Annual Battle of Olustee Re-enactment, the largest Civil War re-enactment in Florida and one of the largest in the Southeast, concluded Sunday, February 15 at Olustee Battlefield Historic State Park on US-90 east of Lake City. The three-day event running February 13–15 featured living history camps, period demonstrations, and the main battle re-enactment. The original 1864 battle involved 10,000 troops and was the largest Civil War engagement in Florida, with three U.S. Colored Regiments taking part including the 54th Massachusetts, later immortalized in the film Glory.

stories.headline: Florida Burn Bans Expand as Drought Intensifies Statewide
stories.summary: Counties across Florida, including Columbia County, continue under burn bans as drought conditions worsen. According to WUFT, 100% of the state is now experiencing some form of drought, with extreme drought (Level 4 of 5) covering 43% of Florida — nearly double from the prior week. Severe drought (Level 3) covers over 85% of the state. Residents are urged to avoid all open burning and conserve water. The long-term outlook indicates below-average rainfall over the next three months.

stories.headline: High-Speed Chase Ends with K-9 Apprehension in Columbia County
stories.summary: On the night of February 10, a deputy working traffic enforcement near CR 131 and SW Cumorah Hill attempted to stop a silver Chevrolet Traverse that ran a stop sign. The driver, Jeffery Allen Steele, 44, of Wellborn, accelerated to 102 mph. Deputies deployed spike strips and performed a P.I.T. maneuver to stop the vehicle south of CR-242A. After Steele refused to exit, a K-9 was deployed. Deputies found multiple narcotics and drug paraphernalia. Steele was booked into the Columbia County Detention Facility on $32,000 bond.

stories.headline: Columbia County Commissioners Weigh In on Fort White Dissolution Proposal
stories.summary: Columbia County commissioners expressed concerns on Thursday, February 5 about the possibility of the town of Fort White dissolving. Commissioner Rocky Ford was adamant the county needs to be more involved in the process. However, commissioners ultimately cannot control whether or not the town dissolves. The discussion follows months of tense town council meetings, including Mayor George Thomas walking out during a December meeting amid a decorum debate. The next Fort White town council meeting is set for Tuesday, February 17.

stories.headline: Columbia County Approves Emergency Burn Ban Amid Wildfire Risk
stories.summary: Columbia County commissioners called an emergency meeting on Thursday, February 5 to approve a temporary county-wide burn ban at the request of the Florida Forest Service. Commission chair Tim Murphy said the Forest Service warned about an increase in fires across the region and ongoing drought conditions. Surrounding counties including Alachua, Union, Bradford, Gilchrist, and Putnam had already enacted similar bans. The burn ban restricts all open burning and will be reviewed every ten days.
